svg.title: How grain number changes the identifiability of G2 and G3
svg.desc: Two contour maps of the loss over G2 (x, kernels per plant) and G3 (y, mg per kernel per day). Without grain number the low-loss region is a long curved valley from G2 430 to 990; with grain number it is a basin around the published G2 924 and G3 8.17.
svg.text: How grain number changes the identifiability of G2 and G3
UFGA8201 treatments 2, 4 and 6, nitrogen off. Loss contours on a 41 × 41 grid of forward runs.
Dates, yield, biomass and LAI
a long valley: many (G2, G3) pairs fit equally well
G3, mg per kernel per day
G2, kernels per plant
24 recalibrations: G2 355–982, G3 7.6–16.4. Held-out grain
number (treatment 6), best fit of each seed: −51…−49 %.
The same, plus grain number (H#AM)
the valley closes to one basin around the published values
G3, mg per kernel per day
G2, kernels per plant
24 recalibrations: G2 831–984, G3 7.5–9.4. Held-out grain
number (treatment 6), best fit of each seed: −7…−6 %.

Conditional slice: P1, P5 and PHINT at the best values of a fit to the real observations (254.6, 954.5, 45.84), P2 fixed;
not a posterior. The contours use treatments 2, 4 and 6; the recalibrations used 2 and 4. Simulated grain number depends on
G2 only, so adding it pins G2 and the ridge closes.
